rationale: The hypothesis posits that microcephaly is present in >=75% (at least 26 of 35) of dominant DEE119 individuals in Leitão et al. (2026). However, the direct data reported by Leitão et al. explicitly demonstrates that microcephaly has a low penetrance, documented as only 2/16 (12%) or 2/10 in evaluated subcohorts, directly refuting the claim of >=75% penetrance.

evidence.text: Leitão et al. report clinical evaluation of RNU2-2 individuals where microcephaly is observed at low frequency: 2/16 (12%) and 2/10, rather than high penetrance.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence and statistical comparison of microcephaly between monoallelic dominant and biallelic recessive RNU2-2 cohorts across pooled international datasets?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether head circumference deviations differ significantly between dominant and recessive RNU2-2 cases will help determine if microcephaly possesses any discriminative utility.

new_directions.rationale: Because snRNA-associated NDDs present with overlapping core features (epilepsy, hypotonia, severe ID), identifying unique neuroimaging, dysmorphic, or seizure semiology features is crucial for clinical diagnosis.
